points: Tell me what you're running now and what keeps breaking.
A rough budget and deadline saves us both a round of messages.
Screenshots or config files are always welcome.

faq.title: The usual questions.
faq.kicker: If yours isn't here, just ask.

items.question: How do you price work?
items.answer: Fixed price per project, quoted after we've talked through the scope. Small jobs like a permissions fix or a single plugin config are usually a flat fee; full network or Discord rebuilds are quoted in stages so you can stop after any milestone.

items.question: How long does a project take?
items.answer: A single plugin or permissions job is typically a few days. A full server configuration runs two to four weeks. Network rebuilds and staff programmes take longer because they involve training people, not just editing files.

items.question: What do I get at the end?
items.answer: The working configuration, written documentation covering every decision, a walkthrough call with you and your staff, and two weeks of follow-up support for anything that surfaces once real players hit it.

items.question: Can you work on an existing server?
items.answer: Yes — that's most of my work. I audit what you already have first and tell you plainly what's worth keeping. I won't push a rebuild if a targeted fix does the job.

items.question: Do you only do technical work?
items.answer: No. A good chunk of what I do is management: hiring rubrics, training paths, rotas, escalation ladders and moderation policy. Plenty of servers are technically fine and failing for entirely human reasons.

items.question: What if I want changes after handover?
items.answer: Minor tweaks during the two-week support window are included. Beyond that, I'm happy to take on further work — but the documentation is written so your own team can make most changes without me.
